assertedAt.description: When the claimants made this assertion. For an assertion they made in a source document, such as a project plan, and that was transcribed later, it is when they made it there, not when it was extracted, transcribed or submitted. It is never the time of an observation, or the time the Claim record was generated, submitted, published or ingested. The same content asserted at a different time is a different Claim. Written in UTC with whole seconds and the offset +00:00, for example 2026-05-02T07:30:00+00:00. No other offset is accepted, and neither is the Z suffix.

assertedBy.description: The agent or agents that take responsibility for asserting this exact content: an individual, organization or community. Each listed claimant takes responsibility for the whole assertion. Taking that responsibility is distinct from writing, extracting, generating, transforming or submitting the content: a person, tool or service that only did that is not a claimant unless it takes responsibility for the assertion itself. A collective that asserts as one body is a single claimant of type COMMUNITY or ORGANIZATION; listing it does not make its members co-claimants. The capacity in which a claimant acts, such as project proponent or verifier, is a role in the context of the claim, not a kind of agent. Listing a claimant records who takes responsibility; it does not by itself establish that the claimant is authorized to assert on behalf of a project, community, program or other party. claimStatement.description: The assertion, as the claimants state it in natural language. It is asserted content, not a presentational summary: changing it changes the Claim. scope.description: Where the judgment applies: the subjects it covers, what it explicitly excludes, and what it does not establish.

unbounded.description: True when the issuer explicitly gives the judgment no limits beyond what it targets, so that an unlimited approval is a stated choice rather than an omission. Stated only on an evaluation without a scope: the two are exclusive.

url.description: Link to a page with more information about the claim. A pointer for readers, not evidence; cite evidence with hasEvidence.

verificationMethod.description: How the assertion or judgment was established, as structured data, so that a consumer can distinguish, for example, a lab-measured value from a self-attested one. One method per record: its party and date are those of the record that carries it (for an evaluation, its issuer and assertedAt), so a subject checked by two methods has two records, each with its own party and date. A value of OTHER must come with verificationMethodDescriptor.

verificationMethodDescriptor.description: Free-text description of a verification method that the VerificationMethodType enumeration does not cover; required when verificationMethod is OTHER. It must contain a non-whitespace character, so an empty descriptor cannot leave the method unspecified. It is the extension path: a method that recurs is added to the enumeration in a later schema version.

wasRevisionOf.description: Identifier of the exact, immutable earlier Claim version that this Claim revises: its ClaimIRI. A Claim has no identifier slot, because its ClaimIRI is computed over its canonical form outside Claim content (regen-network/claims#1), so the value is a bare IRI and the slot names no class. It never names a logical claim or version family. In PROV a revision implies that both versions are aspects of the same thing (alternateOf), so use it only for a revised version of the same assertion; a separate, later assertion, such as a follow-up observation, is a new Claim and is not a revision. The earlier version is unchanged, its evaluations do not carry over, and selecting a current version happens outside the Claim.
